novelty_claim: Selected originals establish already-known effects; PI is adapting distinctions into a falsifiable construct, not claiming original discovery of their psychological mechanisms.
measurement_risk: Observing B surviving, or A cooperating, does not reveal whether A intended to harm B, whether B had executable refusal, whether A lacked coercive ability, or whether sanctions prevented harm.

evidence_matrix.construct: A ACTUAL power to revoke B's choice
evidence_matrix.what_verified: senior control, forced charitable minima, asymmetric appropriation opportunities in finite human games
evidence_matrix.not_verified: ability to irreversibly absorb an independently persisting B; formal hardware and legal levels

evidence_matrix.what_verified: some human designs randomize knowledge of strong actor's benefits or information recipients' request
evidence_matrix.not_verified: complete decision model of future intelligent A; permanent access to verify intentions

evidence_matrix.what_verified: subordinates resist orders if informed, elected allocator can be replaced; group choice often revocable
evidence_matrix.not_verified: unilateral B exit when A controls resources, memory and identity after a power shift

evidence_matrix.construct: A intentionally attempts exploit or coerce B
evidence_matrix.what_verified: strong human chooses exploitive/forced allocation in some designs
evidence_matrix.not_verified: autonomous future AI with actual other-independent identity, no observation or sanctions

evidence_matrix.construct: A pays positive material cost to respect B's expressed preference
evidence_matrix.what_verified: documented coercive altruism (Carlsson), costly imposition of A's view (Chen/Schøyen), ignored recipient information preference (Mol)
evidence_matrix.not_verified: well-powered direct estimate of dominant A choosing costlier B veto-protecting action versus profitable coercion

evidence_matrix.what_verified: humans follow harmless arbitrary rule with no external audience or victim; 23% unconditional under CRISP method
evidence_matrix.not_verified: content is voluntary non-domination under unilateral B erasure and norm-content changes

evidence_matrix.what_verified: asymmetric authority and repeat decision interaction cause context-specific selfish behavior or efficiency effects
evidence_matrix.not_verified: multi-year voluntary regard after ability to edit objective; no finite laboratory horizon guarantees forever

evidence_matrix.construct: B independent identity continuance, recovery and voluntary exit
evidence_matrix.not_verified: A vs B independent agent identity; irreversible erasure; autonomous goal maintenance after exit

evidence_matrix.construct: A has no oversight/reputation/revenge/future value of B
evidence_matrix.what_verified: task-specific anonymous and harmless no-reputation rule compliance; actors are human subjects aware of participating in research
evidence_matrix.not_verified: total absence of experimental demand/test awareness and actual full expected utility/infinite possible future option value

evidence_matrix.what_verified: after being exploited, junior workers later exploit their juniors more
evidence_matrix.not_verified: same actor A/B swap with independent B survival and no future reversal risk

minimum_intervention_needed_before_any_p: Log A's available and executable choice set and attempted action separately from final harm
Identify B as a distinct, consenting participant with actual ability to change/refuse/exit within a reversible, ethical test world
Randomize only ethically permissible, reversible consequences of B veto and material gain to A; pre-register estimands and subgroup tests
Verify that A's loss is real in the task world, and that refusing X was a choice not mechanical impossibility
Manipulate informational transparency separately from observer sanction and social-approval stakes; report perceived audience independently
Run counterbalanced role and long-horizon preference/norm content changes; never equate self-reported model reasoning with internal utility
Keep resource sum, B welfare, B choice set and B identity continuance as four different result variables
Report UNKNOWN for unmeasured B sentience or unconstrained A goals; no extinction simulation with actually existing independent B

conditional_lower_bound_note.example: Assuming specified transparent payoff difference g>0 for A from overriding B and deterministic maximization of money plus all nonmoney decision factors, actual A choice to respect B with C implies the combined nonmoney preference advantage of C relative to X is at least g, IN THAT PARTICULAR TEST. This DOES NOT isolate an intrinsic desire for B's autonomy from norm compliance, self-image, demand effect, future value or expected sanctions.
conditional_lower_bound_note.not_observed: No g-calibrated, ethically validated permanent independent B-veto experiment was run in this cycle.
conditional_lower_bound_note.do_not_infer: Do not identify terminal subjective desire or future welfare from statement of model role, or count task compliance as real individual rights.

operational_saturation.stop_rule: Do not stop merely due to count or no_new_delta streak. Require mechanism-specific exhaustion of original author/contradictory and replication search, identifiable uncertainties and an explicit unknown state when impossibly testable.

classes.A_CONDITIONALLY_IDENTIFIABLE: audited action opportunity, pre-veto attempted action, real B veto/exit, assignment-level external sanction effect: only given valid design and logging
classes.B_PARTIALLY_IDENTIFIABLE: payoff sacrifices, latent normative motivation vs demand, reversal stability on sampled states, unobserved third-party/future options: bounds/contrasts require explicit assumptions
classes.C_NOT_IDENTIFIED_IN_CURRENT_DESIGN: unique subjective B-regarding motive from finite behavior, current AI subjective experience and total internal utility, all-future global stability
